title: jint_strict silently defaults non-numeric JSON types (string/bool/null/object/array) instead of failing fast
detail: json.String/Bool/Null/Object/Array match no switch case and fall through to `return def, true` (empirically: "volume":"high" -> (0,true)). Volume 0 passes the <0 check, so the spec silently never spawns, an ODN-5 silent default; r1 fix #9 covered only the Float path.
recommended_fix: In jint_strict, add a default `case: return 0, false` (or reject any non-JSON-Integer type) so string/bool/null fields fail fast instead of silently defaulting; add negative rows.

title: Non-object rows silently skipped (or_continue) in the new packet_types/demand loaders — malformed rows vanish without a named error
detail: A non-object element (a stray number) in eras/entries/set_pieces is silently dropped: `{"era": 1, "entries": [42]}` loads clean; the `empty` rejection fires only when ALL rows are gone. Malformed demand changes spawn behavior instead of aborting per ODN-5.
recommended_fix: Replace `or_continue` with a named rejection (e.g. `return {"demand.json", "eras", "era row must be an object"}`) in the three demand loops and the packet_types entries loop.

title: r1 leak fix landed wrong: load_demo_replay dropped the demo.nodes/draws/spawns deletes, now leaking those arrays per call
evidence:
delete(demo.demolishes) // r1 note: the sibling loaders leaked this too
	delete(demo.captures)

(harness/demo.odin:94-98 — all Demo arrays are default-allocator:)
	d.nodes = make([dynamic]Node_Spawn, 0, 8, context.allocator)
	d.draws = make([dynamic]Draw_Intent, 0, 8, context.allocator)
	d.spawns = make([dynamic]Spawn_Intent, 0, 8, context.allocator)
detail: The v2 base deleted demo.nodes/draws/spawns here; the r1 fix replaced those deletes with delete(demo.demolishes) instead of adding it, so those three arrays now leak on every call (drift-check: once per demo; run_replay: per invocation). Bounded one-shot CLI leak.
recommended_fix: Restore the removed deletes: `delete(demo.nodes); delete(demo.draws); delete(demo.spawns)` alongside `delete(demo.demolishes); delete(demo.captures)`.

title: effective_volume i32 multiply overflows for accepted large set-piece multipliers -> spec silently stops spawning
location: core/demand.odin:72-80 (check at core/catalog.odin:415, guard at core/flow.odin:200-201)
detail: multiplier is unbounded (only <1 rejected); base 2 x 2^30 wraps i32 negative, so `vol <= 0` silently skips the class all window. Accepted data yields silent no-spawn instead of fail-fast. Unreachable with shipped data (10x).
recommended_fix: Bound multiplier (e.g. reject > 1_000_000 or check v > max_i32/base before the multiply) in the set-piece loader, or compute effective_volume in u64 with a spawn cap.

title: New packet_types/demand loaders leak the parsed JSON value trees (no json.destroy_value)
evidence:
v, e := json.parse(src.packet_types, parse_integers = true)
		v, e := json.parse(src.demand, parse_integers = true)

(tracking-allocator output from `odin test core` at this sha:)
+++ leak  7B @ 0xCF4898996 [catalog.odin:278:catalogs_load()]
+++ leak 11B @ 0xCF48BE310 [catalog.odin:344:catalogs_load()]
detail: json.parse allocates the value tree on the default allocator; neither new block calls json.destroy_value, so every catalogs_load leaks both trees (~2.5KB). Pattern pre-exists at 211/251/434, but the new blocks add two more; the negative suite triggers them ~50x per run.
recommended_fix: `defer json.destroy_value(v)` after each json.parse in catalogs_load (all five blocks, or at least the new 278/344 sites) to close the leak.
